comment: The architecture already provides strong model and terminology versioning, lifecycle states, version-specific bindings and backwards-compatibility policies. One additional permanence property could be stated explicitly: historical data should remain independently interpretable and validatable against the exact model and terminology versions that governed it when created. This is especially important for longitudinal records such as the Lifelong Health Record.

reviewer.name: Timothy W. Cook; Luciana Cavalini, MD, PhD (co-author)

public.text: The architecture already provides strong model and terminology versioning, lifecycle states, version-specific bindings and backwards-compatibility policies. One additional permanence property could be stated explicitly: historical data should remain independently interpretable and validatable against the exact model and terminology versions that governed it when created. This is especially important for longitudinal records such as the Lifelong Health Record.
public.suggestedRevision: Add a principle: "Data validated against the version of a model and terminology binding in force at its creation remains independently interpretable and validatable against those versions thereafter; model evolution must not retroactively invalidate conformant historical data."
